title: Differential defect criterion for an index-one valued point
statement:
Let $R\hookrightarrow A$ be an injective local homomorphism of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Fix a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$, assume $\mathfrak m_A=\pi A$, and assume the residue-field extension $\kappa(A)/\kappa(R)$ is separable, allowing transcendental extensions [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Let $B$ be a commutative finite-type $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] on which multiplication by $\pi$ is injective. Assume $\operatorname{Spec}(B[1/\pi])$ is smooth over $\operatorname{Frac}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\varphi:B\to A$ be an $R$-algebra homomorphism. Put
$$M_B(\varphi)=A\otimes_{B,\varphi}\Omega_{B/R},\qquad T_B(\varphi)=\{m\in M_B(\varphi):am=0\text{ for some }0\ne a\in A\},$$
using Kähler differentials and tensor products [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and put $\delta_B(\varphi)=\operatorname{length}_A T_B(\varphi)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Then $M_B(\varphi)$ is a finitely generated $A$-module and $T_B(\varphi)$ has finite length, so $\delta_B(\varphi)\in\mathbf N$. Moreover $\delta_B(\varphi)=0$ if and only if there is $f\in B$ such that $\varphi(f)\in A^\times$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(B[1/f])\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth. There is no excellence or completeness hypothesis and no separability hypothesis on $\operatorname{Frac}A/\operatorname{Frac}R$.

source.place: BLR 3.6, printed pp.78–79 (PDF pp.84–85), Definition 1 and the paragraph immediately before Proposition 3, extending 3.3 Lemma 1; smooth affine neighbourhood formulation Primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf. Local PDF WANTED; algebraic affine-chart formulation by Q108.

proof.text: Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, $F=\operatorname{Frac}A$, $l=\kappa(A)$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $a=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$. Let $x$ and $z$ be the images of the closed and generic points of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Their primes are respectively $\mathfrak q=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)$ and $\mathfrak p=\ker\varphi$. Thus $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$, $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow l$, and $\kappa(z)\hookrightarrow F$. Since $\pi$ is nonzero in $A$, $z\in X_K$. These assertions follow by taking kernels and fraction fields; $z$ generalizes $x$.

source.place: BLR 3.6 paragraph before Proposition 3; affine notation

proof.text: Both DVRs are PIDs by their definition, and hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. For every $0\ne r\in R$, [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] gives $r=u\pi^n$ with $u$ a unit. Multiplication by $r$ on $B$ is therefore injective: cancel $\pi$ successively and then $u$. Hence $B$ is $R$-torsion-free, and [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] gives its flatness over $R$. For every localization $B_{\mathfrak q}$ the same torsion-freeness holds: $r(b/s)=0$ gives $trb=0$ for some denominator $t$, hence $tb=0$ and $b/s=0$. The same PID-flatness lemma applied to this module supplies the stalk flatness used below. The finite-type affine morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is locally of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth].

source.place: Tag 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat); algebra.tex 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final assertion; Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry/Noetherian.lean:274–276

proof.text: Choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $B/R$. For the universal differential module $N=\Omega_{B/R}$, additivity and the Leibniz rule express the differential of every polynomial in these generators as a $B$-linear combination of $db_i$; the construction in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] shows that all differentials generate $N$. Thus $N$ is finite and $M=A\otimes_B N$ is generated by the $1\otimes db_i$. This proves the asserted finite generation, including $n=0$.

source.place: 07BK (definition-differentials), construction and Leibniz rule; BLR 3.3 opening paragraph

proof.text: The generators give a surjection $A^n\twoheadrightarrow M$ with kernel $L$. Apply [lem-sfb-pid-submodule-smith-bases] with $L\subseteq A^n$ (and ambient module $A^n$). It gives a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $A^n$ and a basis $c_1e_1,\ldots,c_re_r$ of $L$, with $r\le n$ and $c_i\ne0$. Taking coordinates modulo $L$ gives an explicit isomorphism $M\cong A^{n-r}\oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^r A/(c_i)$: its kernel before taking the quotient consists exactly of coordinates divisible by $c_i$ for $i\le r$ and zero otherwise. Since $A$ is a domain, the torsion submodule is exactly the sum of the cyclic summands; the product of the $c_i$ kills them and no nonzero element of a free summand is torsion.

source.place: Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_of_le, lines 492–497; explicit quotient-coordinate argument as in BLR 3.3 Lemma 2

proof.text: By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], $\dim A=1$. As $A$ is Noetherian (Step 2) and every $c_i$ is a nonzerodivisor, [lem-weil-pbc-dim-le-one-principal-quotient-finite-length] gives finite length of $A/(c_i)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] to the split exact sequences of successive finite direct sums. The torsion module $T$ from Step 4 has finite length, so $\delta_B(\varphi)$ is a finite nonnegative integer. By [def-weil-pbc-module-length], a nonzero module has the strict chain $0\subsetneq T$, whereas the zero module has length zero. Thus $\delta_B(\varphi)=0$ iff $T=0$, which in the decomposition of Step 4 is equivalent to $M$ being finite free. This includes $r=0$, $n=0$ and unit $c_i$.

For any $B$-algebra $E$ acting through $A$, tensor associativity identifies $E\otimes_A M$ with $E\otimes_B N$, sending $e\otimes(a_0\otimes\omega)$ to $ea_0\otimes\omega$, with inverse $e\otimes\omega\mapsto e\otimes(1\otimes\omega)$. In particular this applies to $E=F,l$. It also identifies these modules with $F\otimes_{\kappa(z)}(\kappa(z)\otimes_B N)$ and $l\otimes_{\kappa(x)}(\kappa(x)\otimes_B N)$ respectively. These are identifications of finite vector spaces after field extension, not assertions that $x$ or $z$ is rational over the base.

source.place: BLR 3.3 Lemma 1, generic and special differential fibres; tensor balancing calculation

proof.text: The affine formula in [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] identifies $N$ with the module defining $\Omega^1_{X/R}$. For the generic fibre, [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] with $R\to K$ identifies $K\otimes_R N$ with $\Omega_{B\otimes_R K/K}$. Since $K=R[1/\pi]$ by the uniformizer factorization of Step 2, the algebra $B\otimes_R K$ is $B[1/\pi]$. Hence the vector space $\kappa(z)\otimes_B N$ is the differential fibre of $X_K/K$ at $z$. The generic fibre $\operatorname{Spec}B[1/\pi]\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth by hypothesis, so by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] the ring map $K\to B[1/\pi]$ is smooth, hence smooth at the prime of $z$ (take $g=1$). As $B[1/\pi]$ is a finitely generated $K$-algebra, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-dimension-differentials] says the dimension of this vector space is $d:=\dim_z X_K$.

source.place: 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field), implication (1) to (3); differential base change 00RV; morphisms.tex 01UT (lemma-differentials-affine)

proof.text: Assume $\delta_B(\varphi)=0$, and write $M\cong A^t$ by Step 5. Step 6 gives $F\otimes_A M\cong F^t$. A finite basis over $\kappa(z)$ remains a basis over its extension $F$ (expand in the basis and its coordinate maps); Step 7 therefore gives $t=d$. Likewise $l\otimes_A M\cong l^d$, so Step 6 and the same basis calculation give $\dim_{\kappa(x)}(\kappa(x)\otimes_B N)=d$.

source.place: BLR 3.3 Lemma 1 converse; explicit field-extension basis comparison

proof.text: Put $e=\dim_x X_k$. This is finite since the special fibre is of finite type over a field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-fibre-dimension-open] to the finite-type morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$: the locus of local fibre dimension at most $e$ is an open containing $x$. It contains the generalization $z$, so $d=\dim_z X_K\le e$. The dimensions here are dimensions at points of topological fibres, not dimensions of local rings.

The finite module $N_{\mathfrak q}$ has residue vector space $\kappa(x)\otimes_B N$ of dimension $d$ by Step 8. Lift a basis to $N_{\mathfrak q}$; [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] makes those $d$ lifts generators. Thus $\Omega^1_{X/R,x}$ can be generated by $d\le e$ elements. Step 2 supplies flatness and local finite presentation. All hypotheses of [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-differential-criterion] hold, and it gives smoothness of $X/R$ at $x$.

By smoothness at $x$ there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ on which $X/R$ is smooth. Principal opens form a basis of the spectrum, so choose $f\in B$ with $x\in D(f)\subseteq U$. The restriction $\operatorname{Spec}B[1/f]=D(f)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes], part (a), applied to the smooth morphism $U\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, its open subscheme $D(f)$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Moreover $f\notin\mathfrak q$ means $\varphi(f)\notin\mathfrak m_A$, equivalently $\varphi(f)\in A^\times$. This proves the required affine-neighbourhood conclusion from zero defect.

source.place: 01V5 and 02H6, smoothness on an open; basis of principal opens; BLR 3.6 paragraph before Proposition 3

proof.text: Conversely suppose the stated $f$ exists. The map $\varphi$ extends to $B[1/f]\to A$ because $\varphi(f)$ is a unit. On this smooth affine scheme choose an affine open $W$ containing $x$ where the differential module is finite free, using [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension]; the affine open $V$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ it provides contains the closed point, hence is all of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, so this module is $\Omega_{\mathcal O(W)/R}$. The inverse image of $W$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ contains its closed point and hence is the whole spectrum. The quasi-coherence assertion of [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change], the affine description [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] identify the sections of $a^*\Omega^1_{X/R}$, first computed on $X$ and then on $W$, with $M$ and with a finite free $A$-module. Thus $M$ is free, its torsion is zero, and Step 5 gives $\delta_B(\varphi)=0$.

The argument concerns this one valued point and uses finite generation separately for its module. It never uses excellence, completeness or separability of $F/K$. The assumed index-one and residue-separability conditions agree with the extension class of BLR 3.6 Definition 1; no stronger condition on that class was imposed. All cases of zero differential rank or zero torsion were included in Steps 3–5.

source.place: 3.6 Definition 1 and paragraph immediately before Proposition 3, printed pp.78–79
